title: Quantum LDPC & CSS Stabilizer Codes
tagline: Low-weight [[n, k, d]] stabilizer hunts · Lean 4.36.0 kernel
question: How many fault-tolerant logical qubits fit in n physical qubits at check weight ≤ 6?
description: Certify exact finite-length quantum error-correcting CSS stabilizer codes [[n, k, d]] with low stabilizer check weight (w ≤ 4 and w ≤ 6) in pure Lean 4. Every code is verified by an isolated kernel checker proving exact X/Z commutativity, canonical logical symplectic pairs, and exact quantum distance d modulo stabilizers.
verdict: open world record hunt — accepting token donations.

tug_of_war.disclaimer: Counts Lean-verified explicit CSS stabilizer codes vs. Lean-verified upper bounds on logical qubit count k.

impact.ships_to: Neutral-atom arrays (QuEra/Atom), trapped ions (Quantinuum), superconducting qLDPC (IBM Gross/Bivariate Bicycle)
impact.bottleneck: Surface codes need hundreds of physical qubits per logical qubit; finite-length low-weight qLDPC codes (check weight ≤ 6) cut physical-qubit overhead by 5–10× while keeping syndrome extraction circuits shallow enough for noisy hardware.
impact.what_one_step_buys: Increasing logical qubits k by +1 at fixed physical count n, distance d, and check weight w ≤ 6 directly raises hardware encoding rate k/n with zero extra physical qubits.

examples.mechanism: Each verified (hx, hz, lx, lz) tuple specifies exact X/Z syndrome checks and logical operators with guaranteed distance d = 4.
examples.metric: Rotated toric [[16, 2, 4]] (weight-4 checks) gives rate 1/8; pushing to k ≥ 4 doubles logical memory density on 16 qubits.

examples.mechanism: Check weight ≤ 4 fits strictly inside 4-neighbor superconducting couplers without long-range routing swaps.
examples.metric: Finding higher-k [[15, k, 3]] weight-4 CSS codes beats single-qubit surface tiles at identical hardware connectivity.

examples.use_case: Bivariate bicycle & generalized bicycle finite blocks
examples.mechanism: Small group-algebra / twisted-torus CSS codes (n = 18, 20) serve as hardware-testable prototypes for near-term QEC chips.
examples.metric: Every verified [[18, k, 4]] or [[20, k, 4]] weight-6 code exports as binary parity matrices for Stim & BP+OSD simulation.
